Hypnotherapy for smoking cessation shows conflicting evidence across studies. Some randomized trials in hospitalized patients report higher quit rates at 6–26 weeks with hypnotherapy than with nicotine replacement therapy or self-quit approaches [d1, d2, d4]. In contrast, a Cochrane review of nine small trials found hypnotherapy no more effective than other behavioral interventions [d6], and the American Cancer Society states there isn’t enough evidence to show it works [d8]. Other sources emphasize that research is limited and call for more rigorous evidence [d5, d7].

Given these conflicting outcomes, the effectiveness of hypnotherapy for smoking cessation remains uncertain and depends on which studies one considers.
